CORE_DOMESTICATION_QUESTIONS.source: Larson et al. 2014 Core questions in domestication research
CORE_DOMESTICATION_QUESTIONS.use: cultivation can precede archaeologically visible domestication traits; dormancy and dispersal changes need not appear simultaneously

DOMESTICATION_MULTISPECIES_NETWORK.source: Current perspectives and the future of domestication studies (2014)
DOMESTICATION_MULTISPECIES_NETWORK.use: humans act as dispersal agents, selective agents and ecosystem modifiers; domestication is modeled as a multispecies relationship

NO_RETROACTIVE_FLORA_PHYLOGENY.use: H0 lacks explicit flora; R3.34 creates anonymous operational producer taxa and does not claim a 210 Ma plant fossil/phylogenetic history

PLANT_ADAPTATION_GENETICS.source: Plant domestication, a unique opportunity to identify the genetic basis of adaptation (2007)
PLANT_ADAPTATION_GENETICS.use: unconscious selection, reduced dormancy/dispersal and altered reproductive timing motivate continuous trait response

PLANT_DOMESTICATION_SYNDROME_2025.source: Plant domestication revisited: Genomic insights into origins, mechanisms, and convergent evolution (2025)
PLANT_DOMESTICATION_SYNDROME_2025.use: loss of shattering, increased propagule size, reduced dormancy, phenology and architecture are treated as possible outcomes of selection, not prerequisites

PROTRACTED_PROCESS.source: R3.33 evidence basis + Fuller-related protracted domestication literature
PROTRACTED_PROCESS.use: no instantaneous agriculture flag; management, propagation control and selective divergence are separate states

SEALED_ENVIRONMENT.source: R3.33 SEALED Holocene environmental resource landscape
SEALED_ENVIRONMENT.use: producer niches are anchored only to SEALED temperature/precipitation/NPP/land/hydroclimate fields

SEALED_HUMAN_SUBSISTENCE.use: processing, landscape management, storage, scheduling, settlement and regional continuity are consumed as human-side drivers
